gloss: skillful; dexterous; handy; clever with one's hands

definitions.gloss: skillful; dexterous; handy; clever with one's hands
definitions.explanation: Describes someone who is good with their hands or skilled at performing tasks that require manual dexterity or practical ability.

definitions.gloss: versatile; able to handle things smoothly
definitions.explanation: Describes someone who can adapt to various situations and handle different tasks competently, sometimes with a nuance of being too slick or superficial.

notes:
Primarily describes manual dexterity, but extends to general competence and adaptability. The opposite is ⟦{不器用|ぶきよう}→不器用：06642_bukiyou⟧ (clumsy, awkward).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{手先|てさき}→手先：12939_tesaki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{器用|きよう}→器用：02655_kiyou⟧: good with one's hands
- {器用|きよう}な⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: a handy/skilled person
- {器用|きよう}に⟦こなす→こなす：09897_konasu⟧: to handle skillfully
- {器用貧乏|きようびんぼう}: jack-of-all-trades, master of none

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{上手|じょうず}→上手：00707_jouzu⟧な: good at / skilled — more general term for being good at something
- ⟦{巧|たく}み→巧み：07153_takumi⟧な: skillful / masterful — literary; implies artistic or refined skill
- ⟦{不器用|ぶきよう}→不器用：06642_bukiyou⟧な: clumsy / awkward — the direct antonym

CULTURAL NOTE:
The compound {器用貧乏|きようびんぼう} (literally "skilled poverty") describes someone who can do many things well but never excels at one, carrying a slightly negative nuance. It reflects the Japanese cultural value of mastering one craft deeply rather than being a generalist.
